chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Al-Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu Al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) said:

The eating of the catfish (Jirri), the tortoise, and the crab is not permissible. I asked him about the flesh that is in the shells of the sea and the Euphrates, is it permissible to eat? He said: That is the flesh of frogs, its eating is not permissible.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating catfish, tortoises, and crab in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudence on aquatic creatures by prohibiting the consumption of catfish (al-jirri), tortoises, and crabs, while specifically identifying the flesh within river and sea shells as that of frogs, which is also impermissible. This ruling highlights the distinct Shia position that differs from some Sunni schools regarding the permissibility of certain shellfish and amphibians, emphasizing the need for precise identification of species in dietary laws. The narration underscores the importance of distinguishing between true seafood and other aquatic animals that may be found in similar habitats.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Al Amraky Bin Ali, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is not Permissible to eat the catfish, nor the tortoise, nor the crab’. And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the flesh which happens to be in the sea shells of the sea, and the Euphrates, can one eat?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That is a flesh of the frogs, it is not Permissible to eat it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from al-‘Amrakiy from Ali ibn Ja‘far from his brother abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is not lawful to use eel, turtle and crab for food.’ I then asked him (the Imam) about the shellfish of the ocean and al-Furat: if they could be used for food. He (the Imam) said, ‘That is the flesh of frogs and it is not lawful to use it for food.’”
